summary: Defines terminology and design goals for autonomic networking, in which network functions self-configure, self-optimize, self-heal and self-protect with minimal human or central intervention. It sets the vocabulary for later work.

eli5.summary: A garden that waters and weeds itself. This sets goals and words for networks that mostly look after themselves.

questions: what is the autonomic control plane
subtitle: Networks that configure and heal themselves with minimal human intervention.

tldr.problem: Traditional networks require manual configuration and management of every device, which is error-prone, difficult to scale, and requires constant human attention. This is not sustainable for modern networks with thousands of devices.
tldr.mechanism: Autonomic networks use self-management principles where devices configure themselves through discovery and high-level Intent policies, rather than detailed node-by-node commands. Autonomic functions run on network nodes and operate in closed-loop feedback systems, adapting to changes without external intervention.
tldr.outcome: Network operators focus on high-level policy rather than device details. Functions self-configure, self-heal when problems occur, self-optimize performance, and self-protect against attacks. This document defines the terminology and design principles that future autonomic implementations should follow.

today: RFC 7575 is an Informational RFC that establishes the foundational definitions and design principles for autonomic networking. It remains active and serves as the basis for ongoing work in the IETF ANIMA (Autonomic Networking Integrated Model and Approach) working group and related research efforts.

sections.title: The Self-Managing Network
sections.content:
Autonomic Networking applies self-management principles from biology and computing to network operations. Just as the human body maintains temperature, blood pressure, and immune response automatically, an autonomic network manages itself across four domains: self-configuration (setting itself up with no manual intervention), self-healing (detecting and fixing problems), self-optimization (improving performance against defined goals), and self-protection (defending against attacks).

This is fundamentally different from automation. Automatic systems follow predefined rules, like a script that runs the same way each time. Autonomic systems adapt. If the environment changes, an autonomic system adjusts its behavior; an automatic system fails or requires manual updates.

IP routing protocols like OSPF and IS-IS already exhibit autonomic properties: they discover neighbors, build the network topology automatically, and adapt when links fail. However, much of modern network management has moved to centralized systems and manual configuration, abandoning these principles. This document defines the vocabulary and design goals for bringing autonomic behavior back to network management.
sections.eli5: A robot that follows a script does the same thing every time, even if something changes. An autonomic system watches what is happening and changes what it does. Networks should work like that.

sections.title: Key Ideas and Definitions
sections.content:
An Autonomic Node is a device that requires no manual configuration. It uses self-knowledge (understanding its own capabilities), discovery (learning about the network), and Intent (high-level policy) to determine how to behave. A self-knowledge component stores the node's own properties, while discovery mechanisms let it learn about neighbors and available services.

Intent is the critical bridge between autonomic operation and human control. Rather than prescribing exact commands (configure this interface with this IP address), Intent states high-level goals (optimize for energy efficiency, ensure security). The autonomic system figures out how to achieve the Intent. Intent is network-wide and domain-wide, not node-specific.

An Autonomic Domain is a group of autonomic nodes sharing the same Intent. All nodes in a domain trust each other using a domain identity (typically a certificate). Autonomic Service Agents are the software components on each node that implement specific autonomic functions, such as routing or security. They work together through an Autonomic Control Plane, a secure overlay network for nodes to communicate and exchange Intent.
sections.eli5: Nodes are devices on the network. Intent is the network goal. A domain is a group of nodes that trust each other and follow the same goal. Agents are the smart software on each node that do the actual self-management work.

sections.title: Ten Design Principles
sections.content:
Self-Management is the foundation: functions must configure, heal, optimize, and protect themselves. Coexistence with traditional management ensures autonomic systems can work alongside manual configuration, SNMP, SDN, and other approaches, with a clear priority hierarchy: manual node-specific commands win, then Intent, then autonomic defaults.

Secure by default means all autonomic interactions use cryptographic domain identity. No preshared keys or manual security configuration is needed. Decentralization minimizes dependency on central controllers, though some central repositories (like user databases) are acceptable when necessary. High-level abstraction means Intent deals with goals, not implementation details; reporting abstracts network events to network-wide summaries, not individual device alerts.

Simplification of northbound interfaces ensures operators interact with the network at a high level, not at the device level. Autonomic reporting aggregates information across the network and uses exception-based alerts (only important events). Common infrastructure provides shared services for messaging, discovery, Intent distribution, and diagnostics. Independence of function and layer means autonomic functions can operate at Layer 2, Layer 3, or the application layer. Finally, full life-cycle support means autonomic functions understand a node's entire life from manufacturing to decommissioning.
sections.eli5: The network should manage itself, keep using existing tools when needed, be secure without extra setup, avoid needing a central boss, talk to humans in simple terms, report important things only once, provide shared tools, work at any layer, and understand the whole life of each device.

sections.title: What Autonomic Networking Is Not
sections.content:
It is crucial to understand what autonomic networking explicitly does not aim to do. It does not eliminate human operators. Instead, it reduces tedious, repetitive configuration work so operators focus on high-level policy, oversight, diagnosis, and responding to unusual situations. Skilled humans remain essential. The goal is to make them more like doctors diagnosing problems than orderlies executing routine tasks.

It does not prevent emergency fixes. Even with perfect autonomic systems, unexpected faults occur that autonomic mechanisms cannot handle automatically. Operators will still need to intervene manually, and hardware failures still require physical replacement. The network should minimize operational impact while waiting for repairs, but the problem itself remains.

It does not eliminate central control. Rather, it allows central control at a higher abstraction level through Intent rather than device-by-device commands. Operators might actually have more control through network-wide policy than through manual configuration of individual devices.
sections.eli5: Robots still need human programmers. Even self-driving cars still crash sometimes. Networks still need managers. Autonomic means less detail work, not no human work.

sections.title: The Autonomic Network Architecture
sections.content:
An autonomic node consists of several interacting components. Autonomic Service Agents implement specific autonomic behaviors (like routing or security). They interact with a self-knowledge component that tracks the node's own properties and state. Network knowledge and discovery mechanisms allow agents to learn about the network topology, neighbors, and available services.

Feedback loops connect external systems to the node, allowing high-level management systems to influence behavior through Intent distribution. An Autonomic User Agent provides a reporting interface so administrators can monitor the autonomic network and receive high-level alerts.

The critical infrastructure is the Autonomic Control Plane, a separate, secure overlay network that allows all autonomic nodes to communicate and share Intent. The control plane itself is autonomic, self-organizing and self-protecting. It can run as an in-band overlay, over a VPN, or over a dedicated out-of-band network. Security is bootstrapped using domain identity, with mechanisms to establish initial trust relationships when a new node joins the domain.
sections.eli5: Each node has agents that do the work, memory of itself, eyes to see the network, ears for feedback, and a voice to report. All nodes talk to each other through a secure private network that takes care of itself.
